text: Measure the learning funnel per scope before blaming retrieval. Measured 2026-11-19 across every scope on this repo: cms 575 pooled / 41 active (7%), daily-ledger 537 / 43 (8%), ai 577 / 24 (4%), any 471 / 24 (5%) - i.e. 92-96% of recorded knowledge is 'proposed' and therefore invisible to every lane. Retrieval had been under suspicion because a cms brief received 6 rules of which 4 shared no word with the brief, but the 8 rules that WERE relevant sat in the unapproved pile; the bottleneck was triage, not ranking. Two supporting facts: a module pool includes the universal (any) rules - cms reported 104 scoped lessons but a working pool of 575, so quote both numbers or the gap reads as a bug - and only 6 of 87 cms proposals name a concrete file path, meaning most proposals are prose advice rather than machine-checkable claims, which is why triage is expensive and why converting a recurring rule into a gate beats writing another one.
